steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our computational geometry paper on computing a maximum-width rainbow-bisecting empty annulus. Motivate it from obnoxious facility location, survey related color-spanning and empty-annulus results, and summarize the problems we solve and our running times.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Motivation: hazardous facility placement among customers
- Rainbow (color-spanning) regions: definition and the smart-city motivation
- Related work on color-spanning objects
- Related work on empty annuli and corridors
- Our problems and results

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Motivation
  - facility location literature: mostly placing facilities (e.g. pipelines) among customers (points in \mathbb{R}^{2})
  - but facilities can be hazardous (e.g. pipelines transporting toxic materials) -> maximize minimal distance to customers
  - studied: widest L -shaped empty corridor, widest 1-corner corridor, largest empty annulus
- Rainbow regions
  - extra constraint for empty annulus: the two non-empty regions = two self-sustained smart cities, each with essential facilities of each type (schools, hospitals, etc.)
  - -> two rainbow regions separated by an empty region containing the hazardous facility; each color = one essential facility type
  - definition: n points in \mathbb{R}^{2}, each colored with one of k (k\leq n) colors; rainbow (color spanning) region contains at least one point of each color
- Color-spanning objects
  - Abellenas et al.: smallest color-spanning axis-parallel rectangle, narrowest strip, circle in O(n(n-k)\log^{2}k), O(n^{2}\alpha(k)\log k), O(kn\log n)
  - Das et al.: rectangle and strip improved to O(n(n-k)\log k) and O(n^{2}\log n)
  - Kanteimouri et al.: smallest axis-parallel color-spanning square in O(n\log^{2}n)
  - Hasheminejad et.al: smallest color-spanning equilateral triangle in O(n\log n)
  - Banerjee et al.: shortest color-spanning interval, smallest color-spanning t squares and t circles; hardness and tractability from parameterized complexity view
  - Acharyya et al.: minimum-width color-spanning annulus for circle, equilateral triangle, axis-parallel square, rectangle in O(n^{3}\log n), O(n^{2}k), O(n^{3}+n^{2}k\log k), O(n^{4})
- Empty annuli / covering
  - Dìaz-Báñez et al.: first largest empty circular annulus, O(n^{3}\log n); later O(n^{3})
  - Bae et al.: maximum-width empty axis-parallel square and rectangular annulus in O(n^{3}) and O(n^{2}\log n)
  - Erkin et al.: covering points by a conflict free set of objects (each covers at most one point from each color class)
- Our problems and results
  - (I) max-width rainbow-bisecting empty axis-parallel square annulus: O(n^{3}) time, O(n) space
  - (II) same for axis-parallel rectangular annulus: O(k^{2}n^{2}\log n) time, O(n\log n) space
  - (III) same for circular annulus: O(n^{3}) time, O(n^{2}) space; extra case with center on a given query line
  - Problem I generalizes largest rainbow-bisecting empty L-shaped corridor -> sub-case, O(n\log n) -time algorithm
  - improves the O(n^{2}\log n) -time algorithm for widest empty axis-parallel L-shaped corridor

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Most of the existing literature on facility location deals with placing facilities (e.g. pipelines) among a set of customers, which are represented by points in \mathbb{R}^{2}. But there are also scenarios where the facilities are hazardous, for example pipelines that transport toxic materials. steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Most of the existing literature on facility location deals with placing facilities (e.g. pipelines) among a set of customers, which are represented by points in \mathbb{R}^{2}. But there are also scenarios where the facilities are hazardous, for example pipelines that transport toxic materials. In these scenarios the goal is to maximize the minimal distance between the hazardous facility and the given customers. With this situation in mind, some problems have been studied in the literature, such as computing a widest L -shaped empty corridor, a widest 1-corner corridor and a largest empty annulus. For the empty annulus we also add another constraint, that each of the two non-empty regions corresponds to a self-sustained smart city, which means that each smart city has essential facilities of every type, like schools, hospitals, etc. So we need to compute two rainbow regions that are separated by an empty region, where the empty region contains the hazardous facility and each color represents one essential facility in each rainbow region. Given a set of n points in \mathbb{R}^{2}, where each point is colored with one of the k (k\leq n) colors, a rainbow (or color spanning) region in \mathbb{R}^{2} is a region that contains at least one point of each color.

Abellenas et al. first gave algorithms for computing a smallest color-spanning axis-parallel rectangle, narrowest strip and circle, which run in O(n(n-k)\log^{2}k), O(n^{2}\alpha(k)\log k) and O(kn\log n) respectively. Later Das et al. improved the time for a smallest color-spanning rectangle and a narrowest color-spanning strip to O(n(n-k)\log k) and O(n^{2}\log n). Kanteimouri et al. computed a smallest axis-parallel color-spanning square in O(n\log^{2}n) time. Hasheminejad et.al gave an O(n\log n) time algorithm for a smallest color-spanning equilateral triangle. Banerjee et al. studied the shortest color-spanning interval, smallest color-spanning t squares and smallest color-spanning t circles, and gave some hardness and tractability results from the point of view of parameterized complexity. Acharyya et al. computed a minimum-width color-spanning annulus for circle, equilateral triangle, axis-parallel square and rectangle in O(n^{3}\log n), O(n^{2}k), O(n^{3}+n^{2}k\log k) and O(n^{4}) time respectively. Dìaz-Báñez et al. were the first to study the largest empty circular annulus problem and gave an O(n^{3}\log n) time algorithm. Later they improved this to O(n^{3}) time. Bae et al. gave algorithms for computing a maximum-width empty axis-parallel square and rectangular annulus in O(n^{3}) and O(n^{2}\log n) time respectively. Recently Erkin et al. studied a variant of a covering problem where the goal is to cover a set of points by a conflict free set of objects, and an object is called conflict free if it covers at most one point from each color class.

In this paper we mainly deal with three problems: (I) computing a maximum-width rainbow-bisecting empty axis-parallel square annulus, (II) computing a maximum-width rainbow-bisecting empty axis-parallel rectangular annulus and (III) computing a maximum-width rainbow-bisecting empty circular annulus. For the last problem we also look at an additional case where the center of the empty circular annulus has to lie on a given query line in the plane. We solve Problem I in O(n^{3}) time using O(n) space. Our Problem I generalizes the problem of computing a largest rainbow-bisecting empty L-shaped corridor. So we also look at the corridor problem as a sub-case of Problem I and give an O(n\log n) -time algorithm for it. This is a big improvement over the time complexity of the O(n^{2}\log n) -time algorithm for the widest empty axis-parallel L-shaped corridor problem. For problems II and III, our algorithms run in O(k^{2}n^{2}\log n) time using O(n\log n) space and in O(n^{3}) time using O(n^{2}) space respectively.
